definitions.explanation: A type of onion with long green stalks, commonly used as a garnish and ingredient in Japanese cooking.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}に{葱|ねぎ}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: To add green onion to miso soup.

examples.japanese: {葱|ねぎ}を{小口切|こぐちぎ}りにする。
examples.english: To slice green onion into thin rounds.

examples.japanese: ラーメンに{葱|ねぎ}をたっぷり{乗|の}せる。
examples.english: To put lots of green onion on ramen.

examples.japanese: {葱|ねぎ}を{買|か}うのを{忘|わす}れた。
examples.english: I forgot to buy green onions.

examples.japanese: {鍋|なべ}に{葱|ねぎ}と{豆腐|とうふ}と{肉|にく}を{入|い}れて{煮|に}た。
examples.english: I put green onion, tofu, and meat into the pot and simmered it.

notes:
{葱|ねぎ} is an essential ingredient in Japanese cuisine, used both as a main ingredient and as a garnish. The word covers several varieties that English distinguishes as separate vegetables.

TYPES:
- {長|なが}{葱|ねぎ}/{白|しろ}{葱|ねぎ}: Japanese leek (thick, white part prominent)
- {青|あお}{葱|ねぎ}/{万能|ばんのう}{葱|ねぎ}: green onion/scallion (thin, mostly green)
- {小|こ}{葱|ねぎ}: thin green onion (for garnishing)
- わけぎ: Welsh onion

COMMON USES:
- {薬味|やくみ} (garnish): for ramen, udon, {味噌汁|みそしる}, {蕎麦|そば}
- {鍋|なべ} (hot pot): cut into thick pieces
- {焼|や}き{鳥|とり}: grilled between pieces of chicken (ねぎま)

REGIONAL NOTE:
In eastern Japan (Kanto), {葱|ねぎ} typically refers to {長|なが}{葱|ねぎ} (the thick white type). In western Japan (Kansai), it usually means {青|あお}{葱|ねぎ} (the thin green type).
